text: I've always used razors, as I like a very close cut.  I've tried once in the past an electric shaver and since I had left my beard grow 1/8 of an inch or so, it didn't cut a thing and I never looked back.  I got a Braun portable as a gift and I tried it with just a 1 day beard and it worked (never as close as a razor, forget about electric if that's what you want, don't care what anybody tells you, it's not even close) but it was good enough that I could go to work without looking like I have not shaved.  I did some research and this Norelco came on top (second best was another Braun, but it had a washing system with a liquid that you have to replace once a month and that was a deal breaker for me).  I've tried it twice now and is very similar to my Braun portable, that is, just good enough.  Instructions say to use only this shaver (don't mix with razors) so that the machine gets "used" to your beard...which sounds like a lot of crock (don't see any A.I. chip buried in the machine) but will humour the manufacturer.  Anyway, my main reason to get it is that some times after shaving with a razor often my skin does get irritated and some times in the morning I'm not feeling like doing that to my face.  The other nice thing is that on a  Saturday afternoon if I decide to go out, I can just touch up with the electric instead of having to wash my face, apply shaving cream, and maybe getting my shirt wet in the process...much simpler with this thing.  But it really depends on your
title: If this is your first electric shaver

text: I decided to get rid of my last electric shaver (Panasonic ES8152NC) and go back to using a rotary one, so after looking around and reading reviews I deided to buy this shaver.  The good things about it were that it looked cool, it was extremely easy to clean after each shave, and the battery lasts a long time.  The only problem was that this thing can't cut.  When I first got it, it would sometimes pull hairs. I thought I just needed to get used to rotary head shaver again, but it's now been 1.5 months  and it's gotten worse. I have to go over the same are several times and it pulls hairs constantly... I even use the pre-lectric  preshave.
title: Easy to clean but shave was not good

text: First I have to say that my previous experiences are minimal, I used to use razors then switch to electrical shaver under my skin doctor's advised. I was using a CruZer3 from Braun, I love its design, ergonomic and sturdy feeling but it took me very long time to shave and it left whiskers around my neck area. When I tried the Norelco 8140XL just could say whoao, I mean whoao, it took me no time to get a smooth close shave. The things I didn't like were the package, it is very hard and difficult to open, the razor seems very "Light" constructed when compare with the Braun (I think it is more a psychological issue, what really matters is how well it performances), but it amazed me how close and fast it shaved me, even the neck area. Keep in mind that the shave won't be as close as a razor's, but it's pretty close and smooth (No irritation at all). I decided to get this model because it uses the same shaving technology as the more expensive Norelco shavers but at a great price, the major differences are led displays, sensitive adjustments, among other non important features to me, overall it is a great deal. (Finally to be fair, it is like comparing a Chevy to a Benz, both shavers are in different categories)
title: Wow!!! Great shave.

text: Having been connected with the Marine Corps for over 40 years, early in my career I began searching for a blade replacement because I had sensitive skin and was often cutting myself. It didn't take long to realize that with a foil shaver, the slightest rip in the foil could cause a good amount of bloodletting. So over the years the quest has been to find the best rotary. I thought the state of the art had been exhausted until I encountered the 8140XL. Although it doesn't have all the bells and whistles, it does give a close shave having the greater shaving area; gives a faster shave. I am surprised how powerful, yet quiet it is, and always holds a charge for at least 2 weeks. Am most satisfied.
title: Looking for blade replacement.!

text: I've had mine more than 6 months now, and I don't seem to have any of the problems other reviewers have written about.  A full charge lasts about one month.  Yes, the RPMs are slower, and it is quiet running, but I have never been able to stall it by pressing too hard on the foils.  Sometimes, I will shave stubble that is several days old, and it has no problem with that.  The only DOWN SIDE is when I am shaving my upper lip -- if I get too close to my nose, the edge of the cutters will grab a nose hair and yank it out, rather than cutting it. Ouch! I quit using Norelco after using them for 30 years, but I am glad that I returned to buy this one.  My greatest complaint about the older Norelco's was that the blades would become DULL in less than a year, and new blades cost almost as much as a NEW razor.  Norelco has a HIT with this razor by adding 50-percent more cutting area in the triple-heads.
title: Better than Remington and previous Norelcos

text: I bought a braun syncro, after I had my older Norelco Quadra for a few years. While the Braun was good, I still preffered the rotary shave that my Norelco gave me.  I let 2 more years go by and decided to get another Norelco, I still have my old one but I dropped it and cracked the head where it latches, it's still useable though.  Anyway, This Speed XL does not feel as solidly as my older Norelco and it is not as powerful. This gives me a very uncomfortable shave  as it tends to pull my whiskers, it hurts a little.  The Braun syncro is a better razor than this one.  Although Norelco boasts to have a newer and better razor every year, they really aren't any better than the older models, and in my case it's not even as good as the older ones.  I can no longer stay faithful to one brand. I have read some very good reviews on some of Remington's foil shavers and even Panasonic, so maybe in two more years I will try one of them.  You just don't know which razor is best until you try them all... Unfortunately they are too expensive to try them all.
title: not as good as my older norelco 6826xl

text: Before this shaver, I had a Remington trifoil, and I have to admit that this shaver is way better.  It was cheaper, and it's performance is much better.  This shaver is very quiet, gives a great close shave, and holds it's charge well.  I also love that you can just rinse it out to clean it.  No, fancy liquids or cleaning devices are needed.
title: Great shaver

text: This shaver replaces another Norelco shaver I had been using. This one is much more quiet and easier to clean and use. I'm not sure why I waited this long to replace my old shaver. However, one thing I miss is the audible alarm when the unit needs recharging. After reading through the literature that came with the unit, I discovered that this feature was available on an upgraded model; too late to exchange at that point.
title: Great quiet shaver

text: It takes me now three times longer than with a blade razor to even get rid of all the long hairs. My face has less irritation, but having to go through and individually "fluff up" hairs that are lying down so that I can shave them off is ridiculous and probably offsets entirely the benefit of not shaving off the top layer of skin on my face every morning. Additionally, of course, the final shave isn't nearly as close as with a blade, but I expected that. What I did not expect was the razor's complete inability to shave long hairs without manual assistance from tweezers.  I remember having a previous model razor of the same type when I was in high school that worked much better. I expected this one to work even better than that, as it's more modern. No such luck, this new one did a far worse job of shaving effectively than a 7 year old razor.
title: Time consuming and poor shave.

text: I have used Norelco shavers for years. This latest product from  Norelco is outstanding! The circular heads were increased by 3 times  making many more slots to catch wiskers. The shave is remarkable.  Great product!!
title: Norelco 8140XL Shaver

text: I had a Norelco triple header with height adjustment for eight years.  It gave a close shave, but I had to work at it, especially the neck area.  I got my money's worth and more given the trouble free service and I didn't have to replace the blades.  The 8140XL is performing the same in terms of quality of shave and speed.  I expected more given the hype of the triple rows of blades w/in the each of the three heads.  Water cleaning works well.  Much quieter than previous one.  I get 3 to 4 shaves from a charge.  The 8150 model offers a "need to recharge" light.  The 8140 does not, and it just stops w/o warning so better have the charger handy.  Hard to believe that Norelco can justify a higher price just for the convenience of a charge warning light.
title: Expected More...

My husband said that after getting use to shaving with an electric shaver (after shaving manually all these many years) has its advantages. Shaving in the car is great; except when it is so cold outside that the shaver doesn't work, like anything else that has batteries. It does take a little longer to shave than if you shaved the old fashioned way, especially it you have really stiff facial hair. My husband seems really pleased with the convenience and freedom that this cordless electric shaver has given him. Plus it is really simple to clean.

text: This razor is very, very good. The only draw back is that it does not have a low battery indicator. Norelco has a very liberal return policy which is one reason I have always owned their products.

I expected quicker, closer shaves and it takes just as long.  The top pops open without warning and I'm sure the slots are smaller than my previous Norelcos so my whiskers don't get shaved as close nor as fast.  Gee!  Save your money and don't buy this puppy!  I've had at least four other Norelcos since I started shaving about forty years ago and this is the worst!

text: [[ASIN:B0009MFUOA Philips Norelco 8140XL SpeedXL Men's Shaver]]  I've been using this product for about a month now, and it works quite well for me. It's much better than the old razor I was using, which was about 10 years old and on its last legs. I suspect that with care and maintenance this product should last that long as well. The heads on the product work well, and I'm impressed by the science of the development.  You'll get a pretty close shave with this. It treats my skin well. I've had no major nicks or chuncks of skin taken off with it. I like the fact that you can rinse it with water. I rinse mine after every 2 or 3 uses. The only caveat is that you have to leave it open to air dry.  Other than that, it's been a good product so far, and I believe that $80 is a fair market price for this product.

NOW the felling at the end is awesome, my face becomes really nice in the touch. A nice product, I'm really happy with him.
title: Nice Shave and after all you fell good.

title: Always Norelco!

text: Gives a close shave on tender skin with tough whiskers without razor burn. Tops as far as electric razors go.
title: GREAT PURCHASE!

text: My old Norelco was better, more sturdy. This one is lighter - a plus - but being lighter seems to make it somewhat flimsier. Worse, despite the "improved" shaving heads with 50% more shaving surface, the shaving time takes much longer, which took me by surprise. I'm not sure why the longer shaving time, but I sense that the shavers spin slower than my old Norelco. It is quiet, which was important to me, and, ultimately, I do get a fairly close shave. The pop-up trimmer works fine and the recharging stand is convenient.  I like the form-fitted case. The head opens too easily, so I'm forever cleaning up shaving stubble due to accidental openings. I cannot comment on the battery life, as it is still too new to see how economical the shaver is, however I can say that a full charge lasts me about a week (five shaves). Overall, I'm fairly satisfied, notwithstanding the above disappointments, but I cannot say I'm "wowed" by this new model over my older model.

But as long as I'm slow and use some pre-shave on my neck, I don't have a problem.

text: I bought this to replace a Braun shaver that was about 5-6 years old. I've used it for about a month, and here are my pros and cons.  Pros: -I love the trimmer. title: Excelent performance

text: I've been using electric shavers of one form or another for over fifty years, and this one I rate as the best yet.  First it's one of the most comfortable. I can comfortably shave the back of my neck with this shaver where others irritated. Second, it's by far the fastest shaver yet, plus it gets any long hairs in its path. I attribute at least part of its speed to the third row of cutters which sets this one apart from many others. Third, it works fine wet, lotion or water, or dry. I'm using up some of the lotion cartridges from a previous Norelco dispensing shaver and it works very smoothly with them. Fourth, it went well over a month on the initial charge. Fifth, the built in trimmer is effective and convenient as opposed to some trimmers I've had that had to be attached in place of the shaving head. And finally it's easy to clean and packs light and compact for traveling.  The battery level meter is nice for checking when the charge is full. When the battery does finally give up and you're in the middle of a shave the charging cord can be used directly into the shaver to finish, then when ready for charging it can be connected to the charging stand for a regular charge. Charging is done relatively fast also, in roughly about an hour or so it's full and ready to go another month or longer. I have to go over the same place quite a few times, and I don't feel like it is as soft as "just shaved"...  Not as bad as needing a new shave in early afternoon... but the hairs are there... text: I finally replaced my old, widely travelled, Norelco Advantage Shaver with the 8140XL. The table on this page is very helpful, as was Brendan's detailed review. After the usual struggle with the shrink-wrap, I charged it and put it to work. What a difference! I was amazed at the closeness, speed, and quietness of this newer generation of shaver. I consider it a huge step forward from the older versions. Somewhere in the battle with the shrink-wrap, I must have lost the little cleaning brush, they talk about in the manual. I expected to have it and maybe a little vial of mineral oil packed in the soft case, but no luck. However, it rinses easily, and using any mineral oil will be just fine. Also, for traveling, not having to physically switch it to 220VAC is a nice touch. What I do not like: The goofy stand. It looks like some store display stand, and lacks the stability and heft of the older Norelco shaver's charging stand. I also don't like the pins in the charging well of the stand. Flush contacts would have been a better and stronger choice. All in all I am very pleased with this purchase and with Philips' 15% off promotion, consider this an excellent deal.
title: A step up

text: Summary:  After using the 8140xl for almost 3 weeks, I can say it is giving me a very close shave with no irritation, the battery lasts over a week between charges, the trimmer works well, it feels well constructed, and the hot water rinse clean is great.  Background:  I've used electric shavers ever since I started shaving over 20 years ago.  For the past ~12 years I've been using a Norelco 5825xl rotary shaver.  The battery has long since died (I only used the power cord on the 5825xl for the past several years) and I haven't replaced the cutter/heads for at least 2 years.  So, going from this situation with my 5825xl to the 8140xl has been a huge leap forward.  The shave I am now getting with the 8140xl is so much closer than any I recall ever getting with any razor in the past, with no skin irritation.  I've read other reviews that state the trimmer doesn't work well, I use it to trim my sideburns every 3-4 days and it works well for me.  I was a little concerned with some of the reviews I read stating the razor starts to smell from cleaning it with hot running tap water, but I run the water only on both sides of the shaving heads and prevent water from flowing through the entire razor and out the bottom (which the directions state it is designed to do).  This seems to allow the heads to air dry rather quickly, and keeps water from remaining in the main body for a long period of time which is what I assume would lead to the razor smelling badly. text: I switched from the Braun electric razors (last two generations) back to a rotary electric razor with this purchase and FOR ME, I prefer these rotary razors. I say, "FOR ME" because I realize that my own experience may be different from others.  BRAUN - CLOSE SHAVE FAST Both razors are pretty good at quickly shaving the easy spots where the hairs stick straight out (upper lip, cheeks, chin). However, in those easy spots, the Brauns give a closer shave in the first pass or two. It might take as much as twice as long using the 8140XL to get it as smooth as possible. So, the Braun wins the race for getting a very close shave as fast as possible.  ROTARY - BETTER AT DIFFICULT SPOTS WHERE HAIR LAYS FLAT However, the rotaries get a reasonably close shave for everyday use in a pass or two AND they do much better in tough spots where the hair tend to lay flat, like my neck. With the Braun, I would always have a few hairs that would never get cut. They would get so long that I would eventually have to pull them out with tweezers. The 8140XL get's those hairs every time I shave so that they never get long enough to be pulled (or seen) individually.  8140XL - BETTER VALUE THAN LATEST BRUANS AND EVEN LATEST NORELCOS To me, I found those neck hairs a bigger frustration so I much prefer this rotary design and I'm very glad I switched back. It's almost a secondary issue for me, but the latest Braun's (and the latest Norelco's) are much more expensive than this model. As far as I can tell, t

text: On the whole, my experience with this razor has been positive. Although I switched from manual razors mainly because I was tired of nicking myself and expected a trade-off in closeness, my girlfriend says that my skin is actually softer now that I used the 8140XL. Definitely give it a week or two after switching from a manual razor to let your skin adjust; my shaves got remarkably better after the first few days of use.  - Pros: Leaves skin softer; shaves upper lip better than any manual razor; hair length after shave is consistent (including on neck); easy and quick to clean. - Cons: Inevitably misses hairs (although it's hard to tell without close inspection); not quite as close as a manual razor, so you will have to shave every morning if you want a clean-cut look; sideburn cutter not especially useful.  I recommend buying Lectric Shave or a similar product to prep your stubble for shaving with the 8140XL, it makes a small but significant difference in the closeness of the shave.

text: I know it says "Men's" on there, but I am a woman, and I use this razor. I just happen to have very coarse hair on my legs. Lady shavers don't do it for me. In fact, I've always had to use 2 razors, a men's for the legs and a women's for the underarms. I know, more information than you wanted, but it's relevant.  This razor is the only one I have ever had that works for everything. Oh, I had some really nasty razor burn before I got the hang of it, but since then, it's been great! No cleaning and maintaining 2 razors any more.  I have found with this razor, that putting pressure on it is a big no-no. If I do that, it will tear up my skin big time. I have to just sort of guide/glide it over the area, no pressure on it, and it does a beautiful job without the razor burn. Now, I honestly don't know how that would go for a guy and his face, but that's how it works for me on ALL parts I shave.  This razor only needs charged about every two to three weeks. There is no indicator system on this razor, and when it needs charged, it just quits. If you keep playing with the on/off button, it will run for 2 or 3 more minutes, but that's it. It takes one hour (about) to recharge, much better than any razor I ever had before.  This razor is easy to clean, just run the head under the sink, shake the water off, and let it dry out. I do that once a week. Easy peasy.  Like I said, I've no idea how my experience might translate for a guy. I gave it 4 stars because of the lack of a recharge indi
title: Once You Learn How To Use, It's Great

text: This is my 2nd Norelco and I am satisfied with it. My previous Norelco was a 2 row blade system which I had bought in 2001 used for 6 years. There was nothing wrong with my old shaver, but I thought this shaver would be a substantial improvement over the 2 blade system.  The good news is that this shaver is overall better than the older 2 blade system. The most significant improvement is the battery life. This shaver uses Lithium Ion batteries which lasts me about 2 months with a single charge (my old shaver lasted about 3 weeks). When you travel, chances are you will not need the recharger.  The bad news is that the shave, which the 2 blade system did beautifully, is not substantially improved over the 2 blade system. This is not necessarily bad since the 2 blade system was a very good shaver.  If you have the older 2 blade Norelco, you may want to keep it and change the blade once every two years. If you are looking for a new electric shaver, this shaver will give you a beautiful shave in a short duration with a very long battery life.
title: Very satisfactory shave; Not a substantial improvement over 2 blade models

text: According to my Amazon's purchase records, I bought this shaver back in June 2008 and I've used it almost exclusively up until recently when it was replaced by a [[ASIN:B000PKNPES Philips Norelco arcitec 1050 Men's Shaver]] not because it stopped working but because the Arcitec was on sale for a price where it made more sense to buy a brand-new shaver than to replace the old SpeedXL's shaving heads. As of now, the SpeedXL is still in perfect working order and it's likely to be one of my kids first shavers when they are going to need a first shaver (soon).  I am writing this only to testify to the quality of this product. I had no problems with it whatsoever, it never let me down, the battery still holds enough charge for maybe half a dozen shaves, runs as silently as on day one and it's a near-zero maintenance item, requiring nothing beyond the heads cleaning after each shave by placing them under the faucet. The one issue I had was that the skin on my neck got irritated from time to time but it was never anything major that wouldn't go away after a few hours.  Si, it's goodbye to the SpeedXL for me (hello Arcitec) but it's not this shaver's end of career. It's going to be in service, again, in about a year or two, who knows for how much longer :)

text: I really can't complain about this shaver. I bought it in November of 2005, which is nine years ago, and it is still working, and the battery has only just begun to seem like it needs to be charged a little more often (maybe every 2 weeks now - I don't keep close track). Based on longevity alone, I can't fault it.  edit - June, 2019: Looks like I bought this 13½ years ago.  That's a long time. I'm still using it every day, and the shave is still fine. One of the pivoting pieces that holds one of the blades has now begun to pop out of the frame every now and then, requiring me to open the "door" and "reassemble" the blades each time, so it looks like I'll finally be replacing it soon.  As for the shave, "Meh." It doesn't cut, scrape, or pull, and it doesn't hurt. It doesn't shave super-close, and, frankly, when I replaced the cutters after about 8 years, I didn't notice a significant improvement. I did not expect a super-close razor shave when I got it, as I have the kind of beard that produces a five o'clock shadow at noon, so who would really notice if it showed up at 11, and shaving with an electric is much simpler and faster, and, in an emergency, can be done almost anywhere (I was a medical resident when I bought it, so being able to shave in inhospitable surroundings had become important).  If you want a shaver that will give good service, but aren't obsessed with closeness, this one will do the job, and may save you a LOT of money on razors and shaving cream if

text: I have been using a Norelco T370 trimmer for several months.  I bought it for the mini-shaver initially, decided to grow a beard, then trimmed the beard with the beard trimmer attachment.  It did a great job of shaping and trimming, but left a mess of clippings in the sink.  After reading a million reviews, I decided to try the T980 for it's vacuum feature.  The T980 is great!  It does a perfect job of trimming my beard evenly (setting at 7, ultimate beard length to be a 9).  The best part is that about 90% of the clippings go into the vacuum receptical with only about 10% being lost.  I have not come across any of the negatives (adjustment slips, tugs hairs and on and on) mentioned in other reviews.  Unlike my T370, this trimmer lets you know when it's fully charged or about to go dead, and even if it does die in the middle of a session from a dead battery, plugging it in finishes the job.  Most other trimmers only work when charged, not on house current.  I can't think of anything this trimmer could do better.  In my estimation it's looks, design and operation are flawless.  The clipper works well on my beard's 'neckline' and the mini-trimmer keeps the bottom of my mustache trimmed perfectly.  I really think the T370 does as good a job trimming as this one does, but will not run with a dead battery when plugged in, and does make a mess with beard clippings all over the place.  For those two reasons alone, this trimmer is a BEST BUY!  I am not putting the T370's abilities do

text: Ok I took note of the reviews and some issues folks had with this model and I still purchased it.  What is worse is even though I found that I disliked the same things as others I kept it, and only after the 60 day return did I decide I didn't really like it enough to use it. title: Best Beard Trimmer Ever

text: This is a great way to trim your beard. A definite step up from traditional trimmers. The magic in it is the vacuum that captures and stores trimmed beard and mustache hair instead of letting it fall into your sink to make a mess. You don't make your lady mad, and everyone is happy.  The trimmer itself fits comfortably in your hand. It has an detachable cord that allows the unit to be charged. It can operate on the cord or off it's batteries for cordless use. The trimmer is NOT submersible.  The attached guard can be adjusted to 9 length settings with a rotating selector. It can also be taken off for trimming necklines or other areas. There is also a separate smaller attachment that can be used for precision cuts.  The vacuum is power and made more powerful over earlier models through the use of the "Turbo" button that amps up the cutting power and vacuum power substantially.  When you are done cutting your hairs are captured in a removable tray for disposal. There are still a few hairs that don't get sucked up but it a huge improvement over using trimmers without suction.  The only negatives are that the hair capture cup is a tad small. There is also a plastic piece that guides hair into the cup that makes neck and cheek-line trimming a little tricky until you get the hang of it.  Overall a great trimmer for those of us real men with beards. A must have!!
title: A great way to trim your beard!

text: The trimmer works well in turbo mode for my beard, which I keep fairly short.  I'm not sure why there are two speeds; maybe the lower speed is for different whisker types or for longer lengths. I'd definitely recommend starting on a higher length setting and adjusting it shorter until it cuts at the desired length. The first time I used it I set it on "2" which turned out to be much shorter than I would have liked. I especially like the vacuum feature.  Prior to getting this trimmer, there was hair all over the bathroom sink and counter that had to be wiped up after every trim session. My only real complaint is that the unit I received has a flaw in the clear plastic window that covers the "length" number making it hard to see the number. I would buy it again.

text: I've been using beard trimmers for almost 30 years. This is the best so far. Light, powerful and very smooth. I had the prior version which was good, but not as good. I was surprised how much better this version is. The vacuum is much better, the alternate head for detailed trimming is easy to change back and forth, and the ability to use it plugged in is a big plus. The prior version could only be used in battery mode, and when the batteries wouldn't recharge after a couple years there was nothing to do but tear it open, recycle the batteries and throw the rest away (the batteries were soldered, so I couldn't just replace them). Norelco does recommend running the battery until the charge light comes on, and then recharging it (probably NiCad batteries), but this is no problem if you can use while charging. It also charges quickly and indicates when the charging is finished. I shopped around, and Amazon's price (when I bought it) was the best around, online or in stores.

text: If we're completely honest, we've been conditioned by manufacturers these days to accept rubbish without complaint.  Quite true, you can dial into their computer and navigate circles around their voicemail system for a few hours until your anger dissipates.  Or is transferred to computer answering systems.  Whichever comes first.  Happily, however, such is not the case with the Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer.  Not only does this eager little trimmer solve several problems at once but it does so with a composure and aplomb that will sweep away the corporate fog and, suddenly, everything else you own will seem completely and utterly inadequate.  Trimming whiskers used to be such a chore that the ZZ Top look began to show some sense, if not appeal.  The constant recharging, sweeping up afterward, seemingly endless search for single-tasking components that had wandered off and an assembly/disassembly process for cleaning the tool that would make Bill Gates weep.  Philips, however, decided to go in a slightly different direction.  For a start, the battery holds on to a charge with a grip that would make Chuck Liddell cry. It doesn't last mere hours, days or weeks.  Under standard use, mine lasts well over a month.  Even when the battery light does begin to blink, what it really means to say is, "Pardon me but, at some point in the next several days, when it isn't too much of a bother, could you please plug me in for a bit?"  Nothing urgent about it whatsoever.  And once

If you're on a tight budget & can get a good deal on it, and if you don't get frustrated by spending a lot of time shaving the same areas over and over, then this will work for you.  Personally, I now realize that all razors are not created equal, and I'll soon be replacing this with a more expensive model that doesn't take 10 minutes per shave.

text: Although I am definitely on the 'Sonicare' bandwagon in so far as this product's ability to clean my teeth--it does a great job--this model brush is made quite poorly.  The battery compartment (the e3000 uses 'AA' batteries) on mine, regardless of it having an o-ring on the door, seems to be continually wet inside, with the negative (-) terminal on one of the AA-cells rusting after only two weeks use. Philips acknowledges this is a problem but offers no solution.  Also, there are many small crevices in/around the nameplate on the side, and a large gap under the nut for the brush-head that accumulates 'gook' on a daily basis. Philips advises that this is probably 'mold' and the brush should be 'disassembled and air-dried' after every use. It takes longer to do this than to brush my teeth--  Again, while this is probably one of the best ways to clean your teeth at this point in time, and an economical way to try one of the products that normally start out at $64e (and up), there is no reason why the e3000 shouldn't be made as well as the better units, or hold up to water/daily use as well as some of the $9 Crest electrics we commonly see.

text: This product is good while it lasts; it'll clean your teeth better than almost anything out there (unless you have tartar, then you'll need something with a bit more power) and stimulate your gums.  However, having autopsied this model, I am convinced that it was engineered to fail under typical conditions after a time, perhaps to motivate the purchase of a more expensive model, which will itself become useless when the irreplaceable batteries go out.  The first one I bought lasted a year, and even that long only after I learned that you have to plug the two holes in the back of the battery compartment to prevent the corrosion from taking place.  By the end, batteries were lasting one week tops, at 2x use per day.  I also learned that you have to hit it against hard objects when it won't turn on and sometimes then it'll go.  You also need to scrape off any rust from the battery contacts occasionally.  Knowing these quirks, I bought another one and immediately plugged up the holes in the back and put tape around the battery cap.  However, it has now lasted only a month.  There's no rust or corrosion to speak of, however, it just doesn't turn on anymore.  Today I autopsied the first sonicare to see why it had failed (the new one is still on warranty).  In taking it apart, it's clear that most of your money goes into buying a tank-like shell around the $1 worth of electronics.  This would be a good thing, if there were not two gaping holes in the battery cap that let water in an
title: Engineered to fail

text: I wanted to shop around for an electric toothbrush because, despite my best efforts to brush at least twice a day and floss, I still felt like my teeth weren't getting clean enough.  My battle involves bleeding gums, which requires that much more cleaning power in between your teeth in order to get rid of the bacteria that's keeping them inflammed.  The Vitality brush does a pretty decent job of reaching deep into the surfaces and the spaces of your teeth to get them clean.  Licking my teeth, they feel pretty smooth, too.  The toothbrush is recharged with an adapter unit.  Remove it from the base, put on your toothpaste, and turn the unit on.  The agitation has a little bit of splashback to it, so minimize it by brushing the back of your teeth first and then moving to the front; then the outside surfaces, then the inside.  Also, the brush head is fairly small compared to standard brushes.  I thought it was a little distracting at first until I started brushing to pay more attention to individual teeth rather than sweeping broadly across them.  Finally, I thought the timer was a digital read-out; your brush will vibrate a couple of short pulses to let you know that two minutes is up.  It was disorienting at first.  I thought the brush was out of power, but I figured it out.  It's a solid investment, and the good thing is that it's relatively affordable and still an effective device compared to more expensive powerbrushes on the market.

text: My dentist took one look at my inflamed gums, and strongly suggested I start using an electric toothbrush.  I knew a cheapie like this wouldn't last, but I got it to tide me over until I got a proper electric brush.  Even so, this brush was so disagreeable that it induced me to shell out money sooner than I wanted to get a quality brush.  This comes packed with medium bristles.  I was wondering why it was so stiff, but then I went out and got a pack of soft bristles, which barely helped.  The problem with this brush is that it rotates so fast that you have to use a lot of pressure to keep the bristles in contact with your teeth, otherwise it just bounces off them when you use light pressure.  This makes it really hard to control and achieve any degree of precision.  Even with all the extra pressure I exerted, I still had plaque in easy spots that I couldn't reach with this brush.  Don't be pulled in by the price.  I consider the thing dangerous; it rotates lightning-fast and requires hard pressure.  The whole time I used it, I worried that it was going to damage my gums even more than they were already.  After about a week I ordered a Rotadent, and finally learned what all the fuss was about electric toothbrushes.  Spending extra on a good electric toothbrush is worth it.  Don't waste your time with junk like this.

It's way too intensely smelly for me, and just having it in the house in its covered container was giving me a headache.  I took the top off and put it in a fabric bag and put in the garage to see if airing it out would get rid of some of the intensity.  So far, it hasn't helped and now my garage stinks.  This is not what my last lightly fragranced Jean Nate powder smelled like.  I'll probably keep airing it out over the winter and if that doesn't reduce the odor, I'll throw it out and keep the puff if I can wash the smell out. text: I have been using Paul Mitchell Tea Tree Lemon Sage Thickening Shampoo and Conditioner for a couple of years.  It has always performed as expected and made my thin, fine hair more manageable and a little fuller feeling.  The last time I ordered it, however, it did not perform or even smell the same as previous purchases.  My hair did not feel clean after shampooing, or more manageable.  In fact, by day two it looked a little greasy.  I subsequently developed dermatitis around my hairline and down my neck to the point where I had to consult a dermatologist.  She suggested it could be my shampoo and told me to stop using this product.  My dermatitis went away and after about a month, I tried using the Paul Mitchell Tea Tree Lemon Sage Shampoo and Conditioner again.  My dermatitis returned almost immediately.  While I suppose I could have developed an allergy to a product I have been using for a couple of years, I question whether this product sold on Amazon is genuine.  I will not order any more cosmetic products from Amazon due to their self-admitted counterfeit problem. Caveat Emptor.

text: I have a room where the sun comes in every morning, and it makes it difficult for me to sleep in a little on the weekends if I want.  Pros - The mask does a great job of blocking out most light.  My head is right next to a window in my bedroom and I can hardly tell when it's morning. The silk is a nice as well. Getting two of them works for me as well.  Cons - The adjustable strap is only slightly adjustable meaning there isn't much wiggle room between the two pieces of velcro to make adjustments. It sometimes comes off at night because of this. When I first got it and wore it, I became very congested within 15-30 min. I would put it back into the pouch it came in every morning, and I every night when I'd put it on I'd become congested again within 30 min. I stopped wearing it for a little while then one morning it was so bright in my room and I decided I didn't care and put it on. This time, though it had been sitting on my nightstand instead of in the pouch, and presto, no congestion. I have left it out ever since and have had no problems.  Overall, I'd suggest this product for the price. There's a lot of things that could be improved, but like I said, for the price (and 2 of them) it's worth it to me.

Some people talked about an odor coming from the mask. Well, after the first time using the mask I noticed a very faint enjoyable smell, but it wasn't excessive, and was more of a "new mask" smell. It didn't smell like a chemical, nor did it smell like they doused it in scent. It just had a hint of "pleasant new mask" but that faded over time. Definitely not a problem! Although I say it's "odorless" I guess that's an oxymoron, since everything that exists has an odor to it... however faint or strong, or however natural or chemical that smell might be. text: I won't say the product is necessarily bad, but I certainly do not like it and am not pleased with the disparity between the description and the actual product.  While the amazon page says these eye-covers are made of cotton and silk, the product packaging and tags both indicate the product is cotton, silk, AND polyester. I would not have bought these had I known this as my wife reacts to polyester. This just leaves me with another useless set of eye covers that my wife can't use.  Also, I personally find these uncomfortable. The silk is nothing like my nice soft silk shirts. It is still a shiny and smooth fabric, yet also an uncomfortably rough (I'm not sure how better to describe it -- it's like running your skin over tiny closely spaced wires), fabric that is very hot to wear on your face. Furthermore, I found that I got a headache both times I tried wearing these.  My wife has previously made some passable eye-covers out of cotton socks that we both can wear -- and I find significantly more comfortable. She's suggested that maybe she can try taking these apart and using the straps and cotton parts and making better cotton-sock eye-covers. I'm skeptical and am considering returning these. I'm certainly not happy.  If you like the really slick-abrasive feeling fabrics like cheap silks or cheap satins, and if you don't have any issue with the polyester in these, I can't really see a problem with them. They could probably benefit from being a bit larger, but they're 'pillowy'

text: I've used this mask, the Lewis N Clark, and the one that wraps around you entire head, but so far this has been the most comfortable. Actually, the Lewis N Clark is pretty comfortable too, but the dye formulation changed a few years ago and it now stains fabric blue, so this is the undisputed king of sleep masks. No other masks feel as soft and smooth as this one; even the Sleep Innovation (Sleep Revolution?) $25 one that doesn't use an elastic band falls short, especially since it tends to slip around a lot on my (male) head. This mask stays on securely, doesn't stain fabric, and feels like a pillow for your eyes.  However, the sellers of these masks have jacked up the price quite a bit. I remember paying under $10 for two of them the first time I bought this. Now they're edging pretty close to $20 for two and the other sellers seem to be going with it. text: I got an affordable 2-pack of these plus another sleep mask to try. (I'd never used sleep masks before.)  This one is good: very soft and light.  It is pretty good about blocking light.  However, my other mask has contours so as not to touch your eyes: it is wonderful.  This one: just pretty good.  I can tell the difference for "sensory deprivation" that helps me forget about where I'm at and fall asleep easier and return to sleep faster at night when I wake up. This one is nice, but it is only pretty good compared to the one that doesn't put pressure on my eyes (Sleep Mask by Bedtime Bliss).  A warning: Don't tighten the mask too tight over your eyes!  I wore this once recently during the day for a nap.  I was worried about light, so I tightened the velcro a bit more than usual.  I didn't think it was really tight at all, but I guess it was: when I woke up after an hour, my eyesight was blurry--even with my glasses on.  Since strange things like this are sometimes normal if I wake during the wrong part of the sleep OR take a long nap too late in the day, I assumed it would pass.  It took about an hour for the effects to wear off, and I was freaking out a bit the whole time.  It wasn't until later that day when I remembered I had tightened the mask a lot more than I usually do.  I'd hate to think what my eyes would feel like after a whole night if I had it tightened too much.

text: I really love this hair dye. I'd been using Manic Panic Hot Hot Pink for a couple months, and while I always liked the color initially it faded to orange within three weeks, even though I only rinsed my hair with cold water and shampooed with color-safe shampoo maybe 2-3 times a week. This stuff, however, is on a different level. A month ago I put this over my faded out orange-y hair, and just today someone asked if I had just touched it up! The staying power with this is really no joke. I wash my hair every couple days with hot water and non-color-safe shampoo and it still doesn't budge. A few things to consider: it will stain basically everything, but it does come out in the wash fairly easily. For about a week or so it will smell a little like chemicals. Other than those few things, this stuff is awesome. I get so many compliments about the vibrancy of my hair color, even though I haven't touched it in a whole month! I would recommend getting at least two bottles to start if you plan to do your whole head, especially if you have hair any longer than chin-length. Otherwise, this stuff is so much better than Manic Panic, and if I ever want to retouch or try a new color this will be my go-to brand.

text: This stuff is called "atomic" for a reason - it will Not leave your hair. This isn't the first time I've used this specific dye, and I know from experience that getting rid of it takes a lot of bleach, and a lot of patience. However, if you're not someone who likes to change your hair color often, I cannot recommend this stuff highly enough. It's the longest lasting dye on the market, I swear. If you don't mind roots, you can easily go months and months without redyeing. (I usually touch it up every 3 months, but that's just because of my roots. The color doesn't budge.) I've gone swimming in chlorine pools and the ocean, spent days under the midsummer sun, used really nasty hair spray, and washed my hair easily several dozen times without seeing it so much as lighten a little. The only negative, and this I've only noticed this most recent dye job, is that it tends to never stop bleeding. My pillow, phone, nails - they all are still turning pink, nearly 2 months after I dyed my hair. I only wash my hair 1x/week, so if you wash more frequently you might see a sooner stop to the bleeding.  Note: my hair is curly, and very porous. Naturally dark brown, so I bleach before dyeing. I wash my hair 1x/week, and do not heat style. I use only silicone/sulfate free hair products

text: I usually only use konad brand image plates...and pay 7 dollars each. When I saw these plates, I couldn't let a deal like this pass me up. So glad I gave them a try! Wow, what a bargain!  I had no trouble getting the images to transfer and they work just as good as the Konad plates.  Here are a few minor differences I noted..  Bundle monster plates are a bit sharp around the edges, so if you have small children....please take a nail file around the edges to dull them down to prevent the risk of being cut.  The full images are smaller than konad's full images. So, if you have larger nail beds, you may have to complete the transfer in two steps to fully cover the nail. A bit tricky to do, but other's have mastered it beautifully.  There is no paper backing on the bundle monster plates, but to me that's no big deal really.  Oh and one last thing...each bundle monster plate is covered with thin plastic film that has to be pulled off before they will work...again, no big deal really, but if you didn't realize this, the images wouldn't transfer.  I love them! I can't believe the price of these plates.  My friend and Neighbor also ordered her a set and she loves them too.  We can't wait till they come out with a different set...and will be the first in line to place our orders.  Happy Stamping!!

text: These plates are just cheaper (price-wise and quality) versions of Konad plates. You get 21 plates for about $18, and shipping is free, so that's quite an irresistible deal, but I have to say, these plates CANNOT compare to the Konad plates. First of all, there is no safety backing on the plates, as many people have written already; the plates are very thin, and can be very sharp. I resorted to pasting the plates to index cards so it's less likely to slice into my fingers, and to prevent the plates from scratching each other. Secondly, the designs of the plates are not as intricate and well done as the Konad plates. I have a bunch of Konad plates, and the BM designs definitely don't come close. The BM designs are not as detailed, and just are not as "pretty" as the Konad designs (but of course, you get what you pay for). Also, some of the plates I got, seems like there were manufacturing flaws. The designs on the plates appear smeared, or smudged, and when I tried to stamp them, the images do not transfer properly, if at all. Thridly, the full nail designs don't actually fit on your whole nail (unless you have really small hands, or are a child). I learned that if I'm very precise on how I stamp, I can get away with stamping the "full nail" designs from my index to my pinky. Thumb is definitely out of the question, lest you end up with a half stamped thumb, or you're good enough to stamp in two halves (you have to really match up the designs). text: This was my first foray into nail-stamping. I've had this set for 9 months now, and my plates are in great shape. Granted, I made little paper pouches for each one.  Pro-tip! If you place these face-down on a scanner bed (but a sheet of acetate down to protect the glass from the edges!) and scan them then invert the image and play with the contrast, you can get a GREAT black-and-white image of each plate, similar to the item photo but high-resolution. I printed the plate design onto each pouch and that makes it easy to look through and pick out the plate I want.  Pros: 1. CHEAP. You get 21 for less than a buck a piece (as of my purchase time). 2. Comparable quality. Some plates don't print amazingly, but with good polish and speed, they all work well. 3. Variety, themes. There are different designs on each plate and lots of holiday themes and the like.  Cons (the reason for 4 stars instead of 5): 1. Sharp edges. Don't toss these plates in a purse with your iPod or cell phone! 2. Full-nail designs too small for even MY nails. I have very short nails and short nail beds. My nails widen at the tips and my thumbnails are normal-width, and I could not use the full-nail design. These would be perfect for childrens' nails, and I successfully used them by stamping in the middle and then painting a color to each side of the nail where the design didn't reach.  Both cons have been corrected in the new set [[ASIN:B004XJNQXW Bundle Monster Nail Art Nailart Polish Stamp Stamping Manicure

I discovered the injury as he was putting on his socks and when I began to put medication and a bandage on his toe, the end of the toe nearly fell off in my hand. So needless to say a long complicated process began to save his toe; possibly his entire foot. As we age our feet do too. We may get thick calluses which can crack deep into the layers of the skin that are very painful and make the feet susceptible to infection, an infection that can easily become a long standing crisis not just for a diabetic but for everybody when their feet begin to misbehave. Yes, even you! Believe it or not we are still trying to get his feet to heal. Foot Cream of every kind in the house, epsom salt foot soaks,  special socks and shoes. Sizing  It took less than a minute to unscrew it and screw it onto my dryer. There are several smaller, removable rings inside that determine the size of the opening. text: I'm a tweezing/waxing maniac. Although it does hurt to wax, it doesn't suck as much as having to shave all the time, so I prefer it over shaving. The downside to that is that it is so expensive. In my town, an underarm wax can cost $22 plus tip, and since the hair will grow back at different times you may end up wishing for another wax just a week later. You also have to wait until it's long enough too. Since I was tired of the cost of waxing and I don't mind the pain of waxing or plucking, I thought an epilator would be a good buy. I did a lot of research on each type and finally settled on this one about 6 months ago based on the positive reviews. I made the right choice, for sure, and it has paid for itself at least 5 times over by now. Pros: *It is actually better not to let the hair grow long, so that means you don't have to be hairy for long periods of time *You can do it at any given time, if there is anything to pull, which is way better than a once-per month trip to the waxer's shop. *It doesn't hurt as bad once you are consistent with it, just like with waxing. *It is fairly easy to clean and easy to recharge *The flashlight is a great tool to help see those hairs you would miss just off the ceiling lights. *You can use it almost anywhere, or anywhere you have help from another pair of unwary hands. Bikini line, chin, upper lip, underarm, leg, arm, you name it. My underarms and bikini line are my favorite places to use it. *You can use it in the shower *The battery

text: I have been epilating me legs for a very long time & have tried several different epilators over the years. I owned one of the earlier Silk Epil models before & was very happy with it. Since I purchased that one in Europe I was unable to use it in the US which resulted in me purchasing a Remington epilator which I have been using for about two years now. I was never really happy with it, so when it started to give out on me I decided it was time to purchase a new one. I used the Braun Silk Epil the day it arrived & I was very pleased with it. The massage rollers really do make a difference; even though I think I don't feel the pain as much anymore, since I have been epilating for years now. I know some people gave this product bad reviews due to the pain, but regardless of which epilator you'll use; it is going to hurt at first. Personally, I am really impressed with the performance of this particular Braun epilator. My legs stay smooth for about two weeks & it gets a lot of the shorter hairs as well. I also used to have problems with ingrown hairs (while using my Remington epilator) & it has gotten so much better since I started using the new one. I also like that it's cordless & the charging time is reasonable (it usually charges within an hour) & I can get both of my legs done without having to charge it again.  I would purchase it again & recommend it to a friend.
title: Braun Silk Epil

I can use the other epilator in all the delicate nooks and crannies, and have no fear of rashes, nicks, or bleeding.  This one, on the other hand, has left me with some pretty nasty cuts in places that I won't mention.  The obvious solution to the problem is to make sure you only use it on short hair, and to hold the skin very taut, before going over it.  But, sometimes you're too lazy to trim the hair, or sometimes you don't realize the skin isn't taut enough, and it can leave some pretty nasty cuts on you.  But if you're careful, and use it right, it does work well.

text: I've never used a boar bristle brush before. At first I was slightly dismayed at how short the bristles are. I didn't think they would get through my thickish wavy hair...and I was right. But I did a little research and found that they aren't supposed to. This type of brush is not intended for detangling. For that I use a very wide-toothed comb. What this brush is for is to distribute oils from the scalp down the length of the hair. This it does extremely well. The best way do accomplish this with my hair is to separate it into sections, and just brush one section at a time. I can't get over how fantastic my hair feels after brushing in the evening and all the next day. I am attempting to get away from shampooing my hair daily which has left my hair in worse and worse shape the longer it gets. So the brush gets five stars. And so does the service. text: I'm a person that loves fragrances, specially natural oils. I have a diffuser, I add natural essential oils to all my homemade lotions, shampoos, conditioners, body scrubs. My favorite scents are peppermint, sandalwood and argan.  I have tried a few other brands of argan shampoo, and as someone who loves skin and hair products, i'm always on the lookout for brands I haven't tried yet. The ones that work best for my skin and hair, I become a recurring customer.  I have other products from Pure Body Naturals; I like the fact that their products strive to use natural ingredients, mostly are hypoallergenic, and this shampoo is  sulfate free. This shampoo is very thick and dense, you don't need to use much to wash your hair; it doesn't lather - because it's sulfate free. I have no problem with it not lathering. If you think products need to lather to clean, you're mistaken. Sulfate strips your hair of it's natural oils, making it much weaker, brittle, and dry, that's why you need conditioner after a sulfate full shampoo. I did not use conditioner after this shampoo, and i wash my hair twice, once to remove dirt, and second to rinse and coat my hair with the "goodies" in this shampoo; specially because i work in the elements and with animals, my hair and scalp need good cleaning.  My hair smells absolutely amazing, looks healthy, shiny, strong and clean. It brushed easily, no snagging, no knots. Very silky and soft.  I love the pump, a couple of squirts and no lid to close,

text: When I first saw this product on Amazon, I was wary of all of it's good reviews. I am pleasantly surprised that this shampoo lives up to it's claims.  I want everyone to understand that this is, in fact, a shampoo; it is NOT a cleansing conditioner.  In my opinion, that is a plus, as it's important to cleanse your scalp and hair follicles without adding buildup that a "cleansing conditioner" often imparts.  This shampoo is sulfate-free and gives a mild lather.  I feel like it cleans my scalp and hair sufficiently, without stripping.  I color-treat my hair, and this shampoo has never stripped or lightened my color.  As far as moisture is concerned, this adds hydration without weighing my hair down.  Yet, it is NOT drying to my hair as so many shampoos are.  I have long, fine hair, so that's a significant point.  If you read the ingredient list, you will see that this product contains many natural oils and humectants.  Given that, I am continually surprised that it doesn't weight my hair down.  After use, my wet hair feels smooth and sleek, but I still need to follow with a conditioner for detangling.  Again, this is a shampoo; it is not a cleansing conditioner. text: My hair has lots of different kinds of curls in it, from tight coils near the nape of my neck, to spirals, all the way to slightly wavy hair at the crown of my head.  I get a more consistent curl when I use curlers!  I've been using large foam curlers for a while to get large, uniform waves that straighten out over a few days, but I wanted to try a curler that would give me tighter curls.  The Ohuhu Twist Flex Rods come with 7 different curl sizes, and each size has 6 rollers.  The rollers are color-coded by size, so you think I'd be able to find all 7 curlers, but apparently I thought there were only 6 when I took the picture. I'd never used these kinds of curlers before, but they were simple to use.  I used the two largest sizes, and took a small section of hair and put the end of it in the middle of a roller.  Then, I rolled the hair up into the roller, making sure to keep the hair in the center of the rod.  Twisting the ends together keeps the curler in place.  I tried to let my hair air-dry with the curlers in, but I have a LOT of hair, and knew that could take days, so after a few hours, I put on my bonnet dryer and finished the job.  I was pretty happy with my ringlets!  I did muss them up for a nice, beachy curly-wave, too.  I really liked getting the curl all the way to my crown, and how much lift it gave the top of my 'do.  And, the curls weren't tangly like my hair can get if I let it completely air dry.  I could run my fingers through them and get a messy, beachy
title: Twisty Rods for Beachy Waves or Coily Curls

text: What makes fractionated coconut oil different from the solid kind you can find in the grocery store is that it has gone through a fractional distillation process, by which some of the fatty acids have been removed, allowing it to stay liquid at room temperature. It's a wonderful massage oil, with good slip, and does not have a greasy feel to it. I love using it as a carrier for essential oil blends that I pre-dilute in a roller bottle for convenient application. It has a long shelf life, which makes it great for something that will be used long-term.  Above all, this is a vegetable oil, and it will behave as such. Other products labeled "fractionated coconut oil" are often a more processed, esterification of coconut oil, more accurately referred to as Caprylic/Capric Triglycerides. That has a silky, almost powdery feel to it. And it has its place, but would not be interchangeable with a vegetable oil like this product.  This particular product is clearly of very high quality. I have often purchased whatever was on sale in the past, believing most fractionated coconut oil to be interchangeable, but this Sky Organics brand stands out among the rest. It has a lovely feel to it, and the pump works very well. It has no discernible coconut smell, which I prefer when making roller bottles of essential oils, as I want the scent of the oils to come through. Would definitely buy again. text: [[VIDEOID:ffaf5d7e162f6f006c929357f2756230]] Apparently, a lot of the people who give  this stuff a bad review are just stupid and unable to follow simple directions. I received the holographic powder this afternoon and just finished my nails about 5 minutes ago. This is NOT a nail dip powder like Revel. The tiny small jar will probably do at least 100 nails based on the amount I just used for 10 fingers . Steps- You do your gel nails exactly like you always do them, and after your topcoat is cured, you take the eyeshadow applicator, barely dip it into the powder, and buff it over your nail like you are putting on eyeshadow but rub it in really well like blending. You do NOT dip your finger into the powder. You do NOT put it on your wet nail You put It on the dry topcoat, and buff it in, wipe off the excess with a dry brush or a cotton ball, then do another topcoat and cure that. The only reason I am not giving this 5 stars is because I am not sure how it will wear. I will update my review later. Please look at the online directions for this and don’t be stupid! I used several different colors of polish to test it out, and it even works over just the clear. I am going to try it with regular nail polish later and see how it works with that.
title: READ AND FOLLOW THE DIRECTIONS!!

text: Similar to some of the other reviewers experiences, I find that the SnozzlePro works pretty well for me, but I do have to be very careful and make frequent adjustments -- it sort of exploits design problems with the tools you are using. I used it with a Conair Infinity ProPro and an Xtava Black Orchid.  Pros: -It definitely fits my Conair Infinity Pro and probably won't have any trouble fitting other hair dryers. -It's thick enough to be sturdy, but thin enough that I can stretch it onto the hair dryer. - I don't experience any leaking or weird smells. -I can use it (carefully) with the Xtava.  Cons: -It is made of rubber, so when it heats up the rubber becomes more pliable and loose around the diffuser. I would recommend using this with cold air if possible. Unfortunately, my Conair Infinity Pro has a setting for "Cool" that isn't cold enough. So, I find that this works best if I keep my finger on the blue "Cold Shot" button the whole time. -The Xtava has a very short connection point, so even though the SnozzlePro works pretty well, there's not a ton of space for it to hold on. That's a problem with the Xtava though, not the SnozzlePro. In particular, it seems to detach most at the top of the connection point and it will fall off while I'm using it. I just sort of use it gently and keep an eye on that top part to make sure it isn't slipping out.  Overall, I think the SnozzlePro is a great product that would probably work best with a diffuser with a longer connection point t

My hair did feel a little dry for about a week when I first switched, but that has subsided and it's much softer, less frizzy, and less greasy now. text: Pretty sure this stuff is actual magic.  My foundation survived, without so much as a SMUDGE, in near 100 degree heat with crazy humidity, for over 12 hours for an outdoor wedding. I covered some pretty massive breakouts and redness around my nose and chin, and they were still nearly invisible by the end of the night. Even in perfect weather when I'm covering up blemishes it doesn't normally last until the end of the day.  My skin usually breaks out after a day of wearing heavy foundation. I've worn this under my makeup three times now, and haven't had a single issue with a breakout the next day. I'm not sure if it's acting as some kind of barrier for my skin, or it's simply a coincidence.  This stuff is pretty drying, so if you have normally dry skin I'd recommend massively moisturizing at least a half hour before using this. Apply with a cotton ball or cotton round, let it dry (your skin will tighten like you're using a face mask), and then apply your makeup as normal. I'd also recommend a setting spray afterward just for some extra protection.  Because it's so drying, it's not something I'd recommend for every day wear. But for special events or the occasional night out? Absolutely worth it.

No being careful not to touch my face.  Nothing.  This product is 5 star worthy!!!!  It makes your face feel a little dry when you put it on, but it is quickly remedied by scrunching and unscrunching your face.  I apply after my moisturizing routine w hylauronic acid, and allow to dry thoroughly prior to applying a primer.  I would use a moisturizer first and a primer before makeup when using this product, but this is an absolute must for those of us who are oil slicks a few hours into the day.  I expected this may clog my pores or something in order to keep me from getting greasy, but I’ve experienced no breakouts or changes in skin texture or feel since I started using.  Get the setting spray, too!!!!

text: I’ve been using Lume deodorant for a few years now, and I absolutely LOVE it. The new solid stick deodorant seemed too good to be true, so I truthfully didn’t think it would work as well as the cream formula. It actually works better. Keeps me scent-free for two days, whereas the cream needed a fresh application the next day.  I use the Warm Vanilla scent, which is more of a spiced unisex scent in the stick, while in the cream it was nice and sweet. I’ve noticed Lume doesn’t seem to like overtly feminine scents, they seem to cater more to fresh or unisex scents, and I wish they offered more distinctly feminine ones like the discontinued Sweet Lily or Pink Peony, and that the coconut was sweeter (it smells like wet cardboard). I’m not interested in Peony Rose because it looks and sounds like the old Jasmine Rose, which was pretty bad (very stuffy, old lady floral). Fortunately, none of the Lume scents really linger, so it really doesn’t matter. I use the wipes for privates and under-boobs, and I follow with a quick swipe of antiperspirant because I’ll never get used to wet pits.

I am able to kick targets with my beautifully painted toenails about 45 minutes after applying all of these coats. text: i adore this brand because they have the best clear/base-coat ever.  great concept to have substance you are hermetically sealing your healthy nails under have antifungal tendencies (tea-tree, etc.), no harsh chemicals, & some (maybe/supposedly) nourishing components.  strange to say for clear, it is beautiful because it has no yellowing elements - neither when applied, nor over time (doesn't "go yellow).  it goes on thin, drys in reasonable time, lasts well, & even as i reach my benign-neglect limit it still looks good a bit chipped up.  it is expensive, but as i remind myself, whole bottle costs less than the average manicure.  i figure, having that as protective base-coat, you can put any just good-looking cheaper color polish on next.  i was loath to spend that on color sight-unseen i might not like in hand.  finally, i get to this actual color/type, magnetic midnight.  i do like the color well enough, which on a foggy winter day or at night looks sharp, while in sunlight dazzle emerges.  i docked a star because with glitter effect it goes on gloppy.  i like that they have enough substance that you don't have to put too many layers on to give a solid granite/graphite effect, but then you can end up with some sticking out a bit instead of flat as it dries.  great experiment, which i do not regret.  a friend complimented it, & having told her the issues, she said "i'll take it, thank you"

text: I really dislike most "modern" colognes and aftershaves.  Their fragrance is too strong, they never fade away and they usually smell disgusting after wearing for several hours.  I stopped using these types of fragrances upon reaching adulthood and realizing how silly I smelled and how it impressed no one.  In fact, I stopped using anything for years.  But eventually, I became curious after reading a bit on aromatherapy and being exposed to various fragrances that didn't smell like recycled chemical sludge.  So I experimented and found what fits my criteria for acceptability.  What I discovered was that I like citrus, herbs and woody.  I don't like heavy colognes that stay strong throughout the day--I want the fragrance to fade into the background.  An aftershave is preferable since the scent is usually lighter than cologne and slowly fades to the point only someone intimately close will be able to detect it.  Plus, aftershave just plain feels good on my face after scraping off a day's growth.  Florida Water has become one of my favorite aftershaves.  It's light, citrusy and slightly herbal.  It's not feminine nor masculine, it's gender neutral.  You won't smell like an old lady's rose bush or like an adolescent drenched in yak sweat when you're using Florida Water.  It smells clean and fresh and well balanced.  It reminds me of 4711, another classic gender neutral cologne I like, however, 4711 has a sharper, snappier overtone to the citrus and herbals.
